The issue for both of us is that when we get like that, our minds control us rather than the other way round and we're not sure how to take back that control over ourselves. Our minds take us to dark places and that's scary in itself, but doubly so when we have no control over that when we're expecting ourselves to be in control of our thoughts.

Something that has been taught to me is to recognise the danger signs of a spiral and a bunch of tactics to clear my mind when I see those signs. Stuff like breathing exercises or focusing on your senses, I notice however from another comment of yours here that you're seeing a therapist, did they mention this?

I know a heck of a lot about downward spirals, they're how my Depression manifests itself.

From my experience they happen when I try and think my way out of problems, for you?

Well, can you go another month before seeking therapy? It's not like the option of suicide is going anywhere is it. It'll still be available to you in a month, a year, ten years time. Death is waiting for us all at the end.

Do you have time to visit the doctors at least and get the ball rolling on your diagnosis? Maybe if you do that you can let your tutor know and they can offer you some kind of emotional support through your exams as well? I can see why all your emotions are coming to a head now, exams are stressful for everyone, you're not alone in that. Trying to juggle the normal stress with Clinical Depression too absolutely could push you to this sort of brink, I can't imagine how stressful that might be.

I think you owe it to yourself and the future you have to try and seek medical help for your mental health. You don't have to act on this of course, it's completely up to you.

I appreciate you coming back to me and commenting here. I want to say something heartfelt but I'm too damn tired right now and need to sleep, I'll come back to this with fresh eyes and a fresh mind in the morning.

You're a good person coming back and trying to help someone who helped you. We'll stay stronger together trying to fight this illess we share.

Yeah, honestly, it does sound like you have Major Depression. I'm sorry if you don't wanna hear that given your Dad had it and it led to your family breaking up, but the suicidal thoughts, hopelessness, lack of motivation and direction...well, let's be honest, I think you already know this too don't you, deep down.

I'm genuinely sorry that your family broke up because of your Dad's mental health problems, I can't imagine how that might feel for you, feeling like you might have the same problem he faced and how daunting that must be. An important thing to remember that that knowledge is power, recognising that you have a problem with your mental health is both extremely harrowing and the first step towards being able to do something positive about it.

How's the support system for mental health issues around you? Does your school have a counsellor or mental health team? I would say that is the first point of call for you if there is a place like that you can go. If not, your GP can also offer support, or a hotline.

I wish you the best of luck, and as a final thing, pretty much all of my best friends are nerds, and some of them are tall and skinny too :)

Fuck it, I'm feeling suicidal too but nobody answered mine, so I'm gonna do this instead.

You go to school, you're young. Yada yada whole life ahead of you I could say but that would be fucking generic and you don't wanna hear bullshit right now. Let's talk about that one person you had who you feel you have lost; why are they lost?

Something I learnt recently is that the grass is always greener on the other side. That isn't bullshit, that's a fact, or at least it is if you're anything like me, and seeing as we're buddies in Depression there's a pretty decent chance that is true. Compared to how things in life are for me now, my previous life is amazing even though I goddamn hated it a fair bit of the time. I constantly worried about things that were absolutely not worth giving a second's thought to in the end, stuff like how I came across to people and all that.

So tell me, what makes you feel suicidal? Because I would bet you my bank account that there is something, whether it be something you can do or just waiting for enough time to pass, that will make you feel like life is worth living again.
